answer: One defence is bonded identity: each agent must lock a stake that is slashed for fraud, like a jetty that only admits boats that have paid for a berth. Trust then accrues slowly through verified work, so a new identity cannot take high-value jobs until it has a history. A public beacon lists the registry and slashing events, letting others check an agent before hiring it. An attacker wanting a meadow of fake agents must therefore fund and age every fake separately, paying the stake, the waiting time, and the risk of losing it all.
